title: Minimax Honest Intervals for Platform Trials Borrowing Nonconcurrent Controls under Bounded Drift
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS, but paper_score_ceiling 5.8 is below the 7.2 field threshold; the proposed fixed-floor converse is false in scope.
gap_reasons: kernel_substituted at thm:adaptive-minimax-sandwich-sharp-mask because the promised matching frontier became a candid sandwich+separation
The fixed-floor converse is false as stated.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a finite-sample predictable-AIPW upper bound, an optimized observed-law lower envelope, a sharp continuum-mask certificate, and a rare-history separation showing that the AIPW radius need not match unrestricted minimax interval length. The promised matching all-kernel frontier collapsed: even a common propensity floor can allow L*=0 while the clipped AIPW radius is 2M, so the proposed finite-constant converse is false in the stated class. A narrower regime with additional information/reachability structure would need genuinely new theory rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: For the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm effect, the exact cumulative-discrepancy program gives the sharp bounded-drift borrowing bias, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope. The projected interval is uniformly design-honest and has worst-case expected length at most twice the clipped optimized radius. The all-kernel lower side is the optimized observed-law total-variation envelope \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\sup_{0\le\eta<1-2\alpha}(1-2\alpha-\eta)\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta)\), with the fixed \(\eta_\alpha\) bound as a corollary. A continuum of schedules sharing each masked-history restriction yields the computable sharp certificate \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\max_S2Mw(S)[q_S-\alpha]_+\). This is an adaptive minimax sandwich, not a matching frontier: an explicit positive-per-experiment three-block sequence has \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) and ratio at most \(2(1-\alpha/2)/\sqrt{n\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\). The fixed-common-floor comparison remains an unanswered, nondependent question.
gap: LeeWason2020 directly compares all versus concurrent controls in a two-stage adding-arm platform under parametric linear and step trends and reports stage-adjustment equivalence with concurrent-only analysis. BofillRoigEtAl2022 and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift analyze fixed, mixed, or spline time-trend adjustments through model-based bias, type-I error, and power, MarschnerSchou2024 analyzes randomized-cohort adjustment, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 gives a superpopulation efficiency analysis of the concurrent estimand. ChenLiZhangYe2025 Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and attaining upper construction for bounded-confounding Gaussian RCT and observational summaries; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility. The literature lacks a best uniformly honest fixed-schedule randomization interval under a total-variation calendar-drift class, observed-data measurability, and unequal adaptive-history probabilities.
fill: The formal program consists of the cumulative-sum bias dual, an everywhere-nonempty projected AIPW interval, a matching observed-law mixture lower bound over every schedule-independent randomized interval kernel through a sequential likelihood-ratio or deficiency construction, a pointwise AIPW optimizer certificate, exact full-data versus concurrent-only minimax equality at vacuous drift, and a three-block reduction whose zero-drift value has an explicit primal--dual certificate.
